meta.title: Missale: Catholic prayer app for iPhone and iPad
meta.description: The Word, a saint and the Rosary each day, and a simple routine with God from morning to night. A Catholic app for iPhone and iPad, in 3 languages.
meta.ogAlt: Missale, a place to reflect on your day and give thanks, on a parchment-colored background.

cta.soon: Coming soon to the App Store

hero.title: A place to reflect on your day and give thanks.
hero.subtitle: The Word, a saint and the Rosary each day, and a simple routine with God: morning, afternoon and night.

line.neutral: Morning, afternoon and night: a day with God.
line.morning: Begin by offering the day and opening today's Word.
line.afternoon: Pause for a moment to say how you are.
line.night: Look back on the day and give thanks.

video.caption: A 25-second video without sound showing the app in use: the Today screen, the "Today I am…" check-in with its response, and the evening Examen.

day.title: Morning, afternoon and night, one step at a time.
day.intro: Missale shapes the day into simple moments. Do what you can, at your own pace.

morning.label: Morning
morning.title: Offer the day and open the Word
morning.body: Start with the morning offering, writing what you hope for from the day, and read the Word of the day with its context.
morning.alt: The Today screen in Missale, with the "Your day with God" list and the steps of the daily routine.

afternoon.label: Afternoon
afternoon.title: Say how you are
afternoon.body: In the "Today I am…" check-in, pick one of 16 states and write a few words if you like.
afternoon.alt: The check-in screen, with the 16 states to choose from.

night.label: Night
night.title: Look back and give thanks
night.body: The evening Examen returns to what you wrote in the morning. Then pray Compline, the night prayer.
night.alt: The evening Examen screen, in dark tones, with the questions for looking back on the day.

gratitude.question: What would you like to give thanks for today?

features.title: To pray, read and learn, every day.
features.intro: Five parts of the app to get to know.

word.title: Word and Saint of the day
word.body: The Word of the day with context, and the saint of the day with a biography and a prayer. Both are available as widgets on your iPhone home screen.
word.alt: The Saint of the day screen in Missale, with the saint's name, public-domain art and biography.

rosary.title: Guided Rosary
rosary.body: Pray with a voice guiding you, in beginner mode or with the screen off, and keep your phone in your pocket.
rosary.alt: The Rosary screen in Missale, showing a Hail Mary.

checkin.title: Today I am…
checkin.body: Pick one of 16 states and receive a Psalm, a saint and a step for the day. What you write stays on your device unless you tap to receive guidance.
checkin.alt: The "Today I am…" check-in screen, with the 16 states.

bible.title: The Bible in your language
bible.body: The complete Bible, with bookmarks, search by reference or word, and the place where you left off.
bible.alt: The Bible screen in Missale, with a Psalm open.

formation.title: Formation
formation.body: Seven paths with 50 short lessons, about 4 minutes each, on the Mass, the sacraments, the liturgical year and more.

guidance.title: The AI chooses from the collection and writes a short reflection.
guidance.intro: Guidance starts from what you write. One AI chooses, among Catholic responses that have already been reviewed, the Psalm, the saint and the step. Another writes a short reflection from them.

steps.title: You write
steps.body: Say in your own words what you are feeling.

steps.title: The app chooses
steps.body: From 720 reviewed Catholic responses, 240 per language, an AI picks the one that fits your text best.

steps.title: You receive
steps.body: A Psalm, a saint who went through something similar, one concrete step for the day, and a short reflection written by AI from them.

guidance.care: If what you write shows a sign of risk to life, the app shows crisis guidance first.
guidance.disclaimer: Missale does not replace a priest, a spiritual director or professional care.

privacy.title: Your day is yours.
privacy.lead: What you write stays on your phone.

exceptions.title: Guidance
exceptions.body: The text you write leaves your device only when you tap the button to receive guidance. It goes to AI services from other companies, which choose the response from the collection and write the reflection. We do not store that text.

exceptions.title: Personalization
exceptions.body: For subscribers with personalization turned on, a few texts are sent out to choose what to show: the Rosary intention, your Examen answers, the morning intention and, for the Word of the day, your latest "Today I am…" entry. This only starts after you allow it, and you can turn it off in Settings. Here the text is used only to choose something from the reviewed collection.

points: You can export and delete your data at any time.
You sign in with Apple, with no password.
No ads. We do not sell, rent or share data.

pricing.title: The essentials are free.
pricing.intro: Start for free and, if you want more, try Premium.

free.title: Free forever
items: The complete Rosary: guided, with voice, beginner mode and screen-off mode
The "Today I am…" check-in with all support resources

premium.title: Premium
premium.tagline: To go deeper into the routine.

pricing.trial: 14 days free, monthly or yearly plan. The free period applies once per Apple ID.
pricing.priceNote: See the price on the App Store. Prices vary by country.

items.q: Which languages is Missale available in?
items.a: English, Portuguese and Spanish. Each language has its own texts, not an automatic translation.

items.q: Which Bible does the app use?
items.a: A complete Bible in a public-domain Catholic edition: Douay-Rheims in English, Matos Soares in Portuguese and Torres Amat in Spanish.
Yes. The app asks for an account, created with Sign in with Apple. There is no password: Apple confirms that it is you.

items.q: Does it work on iPad and Android?
items.a: Missale is available for iPhone and iPad. There is no Android version yet.

items.q: Where does the content come from?
items.a: From Catholic and public-domain sources, always with the reference. In guidance, the Psalm, the saint and the step come from a reviewed collection, and the short reflection that goes with them is written by AI. New content arrives without you having to update the app.

footer.line: Missale is a prayer companion; it does not replace the sacramental life of the Church.

support.title: Support
support.description: Help with Missale: your subscription, exporting and deleting your data, and common questions.
support.intro: Write to us and we will reply by email.

sections.title: Manage or cancel your subscription
body: The subscription is managed in your Apple account: iPhone Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions.
To avoid being charged for the next period, cancel at least 24 hours before the current period ends.

sections.title: Export your data
body: In the app, open Settings › Your data and tap Export your data.
You get a JSON file with everything you wrote and logged, through the iOS share sheet. The file is made on your device and only leaves it if you send it.

sections.title: Delete your data and account
body: To delete what you wrote and logged on your device, open Settings › Your data and tap Delete your data. Your preferences stay. This cannot be undone.
To delete your account, open Settings › Account › Delete account, or write to the support email. This erases from our server what we keep about you.
Deleting the account does not cancel the subscription. That is done in the App Store.

sections.title: Common questions
body: Changed devices? Restore your purchase on the new device, signing in with the same Apple ID.
Saints, words of the day and other new content arrive without you having to update the app.
